assetNeeds.reason: Rotoscoping means tracing filmed movement. No footage was supplied, and the available tools cannot film or create real live-action footage.
assetNeeds.question: Can you supply a short clip or numbered frames of someone reaching forward, so the trace can follow real footage?
assetNeeds.fallback: The figure follows a hand-keyed joint track based on how people reach, with a simulated reference plate. This is disclosed as a reconstruction, not a trace of real footage.

displayDescription: A traced figure reaches out on a cool light table; its hand becomes the first vertex of a connected node system.
styleRenderer: Canvas 2D (traced figure, simulated reference plate, network)
SVG (stationary light-table cel border, peg bar, registration marks)
motionEngine: GSAP paused timeline at window.__timelines.video (sole owner of all animated scalars; Canvas redraws from them on update and hf-seek)
audioDescription: Silent preview: no audio track, music, voice or sound effects.
limitations: No live-action footage was supplied, and the available tools cannot film any, so nothing here was traced from real footage. The reach comes from a hand-keyed joint track (lean, upper-arm, forearm and rear-arm angles) based on how people reach. It reconstructs rotoscoping's look and trace-over-plate workflow but is not true rotoscoping.
The soft 'reference plate' silhouette is simulated from the same joint track, not filmed footage.
Traced drawings are held for 2 frames (15 drawings/s) at 30 fps delivery; the plate runs continuously to show the trace snapping to it.
Torso lean is approximated by a 2D shear about the feet line; no 3D body or lighting.

Scene palette: cool light-table #E3E9EA chosen instead of the earlier warm #F1EBDD; ink #314249 and Fill A #9D8A72 keep their earlier roles. Ink on table contrast is 8.53:1. Fill A on table is 2.71:1, so it is used only for decoration and fills, never for text.
